page: Microsoft Azure FX16mds_v2 is a memory-intensive virtual server belonging to the FXmdsv2 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is equipped with an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs, which map to 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a high clock speed of 4.2 GHz and is supported by a substantial cache hierarchy, including a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. The server is provisioned with 336.0 GB of system memory, yielding an exceptionally high allocation of 21.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage consists of a 945 GB disk, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPU accelerators are present on this configuration.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong single-core capabilities. It achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 2217.0 and a single-threaded gzip compression speed of 34.55 GB/sec, both of which rank in the top 25% of tested hardware. Text processing performance is top-tier, scoring 2988.0 on Geekbench, which places it in the top 10%. Additionally, its LLM inference speed for text generation using a small 135M model is highly efficient at 429.6 tokens/sec, also landing in the top 10%. Conversely, multi-core metrics such as stress-ng multi-core performance and Geekbench multi-core scores fall within the average range. A notable tradeoff is the Passmark memory score of 1795.91, which sits in the bottom 25%, indicating lower relative performance in specific memory-bound synthetic tests despite the large capacity.

The qualitative cost profile of the FX16mds_v2 reflects its specialized hardware density, trading massive RAM capacity and high CPU clock speeds for standard multi-core scaling. This resource distribution makes the server highly effective for workloads that require large memory footprints but do not scale linearly across massive core counts. It is a precise fit for memory-intensive database operations, text processing pipelines, single-threaded data compression tasks, and small-scale language model inference.
